surface: POST dispatchUrl with {dispatch: StandardRailDispatchV2, quote: QuoteV1, request, evidenceBundle}; answer {taskId, dispatchHash, signature, state, operations} plus terminalAttestation for completed, failed and canceled
signature: signature: EIP-191 by the provider authority key over keccak256(canonicalJson({taskId, dispatchHash, state, operations})); terminalAttestation.signature: EIP-191 by the terminal attestation key over keccak256(canonicalJson(payload)), payload {taskId, dispatchHash, state, resultHash, completedAt}

verdicts.accepted: The gateway resolves the dispatch to the task and moves the order to orderStateAfter.
verdicts.refused: Definite refusal before admission: the gateway records it and later sends a fresh envelope with a new nonce.
verdicts.ambiguous: The gateway cannot trust the answer and polls dispatch status for the original dispatch hash.

initial.purpose: The first dispatch of the paid order in context.json.

responses.purpose: An admitted dispatch answered submitted: no attestation, all-null operations at revision 0.
An admitted dispatch answered working: no attestation, all-null operations at revision 0.
An admitted dispatch answered input-required: no attestation, all-null operations at revision 0.
A synchronous completion: the dispatch attestation binds the frozen result's hash; the result itself is not inline.
A synchronous failure is attested like a completion.
Operations observed 300 s before receipt are fresh.
Operations observed 301 s before receipt are refused.
Operations observed 30 s after receipt are fresh.
Operations observed 31 s after receipt are refused.
A definite refusal before any admission: the gateway records it and later sends a fresh envelope.
A synchronous provider that cannot execute yet refuses before admission.
An empty 503 is the deliberate ambiguous answer: the gateway polls status for the original hash.
JSON without an error key proves nothing.
A null error proves nothing.
An edge or proxy page proves nothing.
A 2xx carrying an error is not a refusal and not a valid answer.
The internal executing state is never a wire state.
A dispatch answer never carries the result inline.
Exactly the accepted keys.
operations is required.
A terminal state requires its attestation.
Only terminal states carry an attestation.
The answer must name the dispatch hash it was asked for.
The answer is signed by the provider authority key.
The signature covers taskId, dispatchHash, state and operations.
The signature covers the operations.
taskId is 1 to 128 characters.
Terminal attestations are signed by the terminal attestation key.
The attestation names the answer's state.
completedAt may lead the gateway's clock by at most 30 seconds.
The attestation signature covers its whole payload.
Cross-type reuse: a lifecycle attestation (orderId instead of dispatchHash) is not a dispatch attestation.
Cross-type reuse: a signed quote answer is not a dispatch answer.
A body with a duplicate key is refused.
A compressed body is refused before it is read.
Only application/json is read.
